lessons.title: ସ୍ୱର · Vowels
lessons.subtitle: Odia's round vowels — the ସ୍ୱର, eleven in all
lessons.content:
# ସ୍ୱର (Vowels)

Odia uses the **Odia script** — the roundest of all Indian scripts,
evolved from writing on palm leaves with an iron stylus (curves, never
straight lines). Its vowels are **ସ୍ୱର**.

## The vowel set

| Vowel | Roman | Example | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| ଅ | a | ଅମ୍ବ | mango |
| ଆ | ā | ଆମେ | we |
| ଇ | i | ଇଣ୍ଟା | brick |
| ଈ | ī | ଈଶ୍ୱର | God |
| ଉ | u | ଉଷା | dawn |
| ଊ | ū | ଊଟି | nap |
| ଋ | r̥ | ଋଷି | sage |
| ଏ | e | ଏଠାରେ | here |
| ଐ | ai | ଐରାବତ | airavata |
| ଓ | o | ଓଡ଼ିଆ | Odia |
| ଔ | au | ଔଷଧ | medicine |

Note: Odia has **ଏ** and **ଓ** as simple e/o (the ଐ/ଔ are diphthongs).
This makes the vowel chart smaller than Hindi's — eleven, not thirteen.

## Short vs long

Length matters: **ମାନେ** (māne, means) vs **ମନେ** (mane, to the
mind) differ only in that held ଆ. Hold the long vowel a full beat.

## Reading habit

Letters hang from a rounded top curl. Vowels standing alone begin
words; inside words they become **ମାତ୍ରା** signs attached to
consonants — next lesson.
## Mini-practice

Cover the Roman column and read: ଅମ୍ବ (amba, mango), ଆମେ (āmē, we),
ଇଣ୍ଟା (iṇṭā, brick), ଉଷା (uṣā, dawn), ଏଠାରେ (eṭhāre, here),
ଓଡ଼ିଆ (oṛiā, Odia). Then reverse: long ā → ଆ. Eleven vowels, one
held-beat rule — say ମାନେ and ମନେ back to back until your ear
catches the difference.

lessons.title: ବ୍ୟଞ୍ଜନ · Consonants
lessons.subtitle: The consonant grid and Odia's signature ଡ଼ / ଢ଼ sounds
lessons.content:
# ବ୍ୟଞ୍ଜନ (Consonants)

Odia consonants (**ବ୍ୟଞ୍ଜନ**) sit in the same Dravidian-era grid as its
cousins. Each bare letter reads consonant + ଅ: **କ** = "ka".

## The grid

| | Voiceless | Aspirated | Voiced | Voiced asp. | Nasal |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Velar | କ ka | ଖ kha | ଗ ga | ଘ gha | ଙ ṅa |
| Palatal | ଚ cha | ଛ chha | ଜ ja | ଝ jha | ଞ nya |
| Retroflex | ଟ ṭa | ଠ ṭha | ଡ ḍa | ଢ ḍha | ଣ ṇa |
| Dental | ତ ta | ଥ tha | ଦ da | ଧ dha | ନ na |
| Labial | ପ pa | ଫ pha | ବ ba | ଭ bha | ମ ma |

## The "others" rows

| Letters | Sounds |
|---|---|
| ଯ ର ଲ ଵ | ya, ra, la, va |
| ଶ ଷ ସ ହ | śa, ṣa, sa, ha |
| ଳ | retroflex ḷ |
| ୟ | ya (special form) |

## The flapped ଡ଼ and ଢ଼

Two letters are dotted versions: **ଡ଼** (ṛa) and **ଢ଼** (ṛha) — flapped
r-like sounds, and they are *everywhere*: **ଓଡ଼ିଆ** (Oṛiā, the language
name itself!), **ଡ଼ାଲି** (ṛāli, ladle) and
**ଢ଼େଣୁ** (ṛheṇu, fly). The dot is not decoration; dropping it
changes the letter to ଡ/ଢ and the meaning goes wrong.

> Compare: **ର** (ra, tooth-r) in **ରାଜା** (rājā, king) vs **ଡ଼** (ṛa,
> flap) in **ଓଡ଼ିଆ**. Two r-sounds, both essential.
## Mini-practice

Read aloud: କମଳ (kamaḷa, lotus), ଗଜ (gaja, elephant), ବର୍ଷା
(barṣā, rain), ବାଘ (bāgha, tiger), ହାତ (hāta, hand).
Then the flap drill: ରାଜା (rājā, ra) vs ଓଡ଼ିଆ (oṛiā, ṛa) — plain
tooth-r vs dotted flap. The dot is tiny; the sound is a different
letter. Train it in the language's own name.

lessons.title: ମାତ୍ରା · Vowel Signs
lessons.subtitle: Consonant + matra — how Odia words actually get written
lessons.content:
# ମାତ୍ରା (Vowel Signs)

A bare consonant **କ** says "ka". Attach a **ମାତ୍ରା** (vowel sign) and
the vowel changes.

## The pattern on କ

| Sign | Result | Sound |
|---|---|---|
| (none) | କ | ka |
| ା | କା | kā |
| ି | କି | ki |
| ୀ | କୀ | kī |
| ୁ | କୁ | ku |
| ୂ | କୂ | kū |
| େ | କେ | ke |
| ୈ | କୈ | kai |
| ୋ | କୋ | ko |
| ୌ | କୌ | kau |

## The left-side signs

**ି** (i-sign) attaches on the *left* of the consonant though it is
pronounced *after*: **କି** reads "ki". Words like **କିମ୍ବା** (kimbā, or)
and **ମିଠା** (miṭhā, sweet) show it: the ି sits before ମ
but sounds after it. Sign
order ≠ reading order — the classic trap, same as Kannada.

## The anusvāra and visarga

**ଂ** adds a nasal m/n sound at the syllable end: **ଅଂଶ** (aṃśa, part). **ଃ** is a faint h: **ଦୁଃଖ** (dukha, sorrow).
Both appear constantly in real text.

> The **ୟ**, **ୱ** special forms and the conjunct **୍ର** (ra-matra)
> show up in words like **ପ୍ରାର୍ଥନା** — read clusters slowly.
## Mini-practice

Read: କିମ୍ବା (kimbā, or), ଗୁଡ଼ା (guḍā, jaggery), କୋଟ (koṭa,
fort), ନଦୀ (nadī, river), ମୁଣ୍ଡ (muṇḍa, head). Then split ପୁସ୍ତକ letter by letter: ପୁ-ସ୍-ତ-କ. Note
the left-side ି in କି — sign on the left, sound after the
consonant.

lessons.title: ଯୁକ୍ତାକ୍ଷର · Conjuncts
lessons.subtitle: Two consonants, one shape — the conjunct system
lessons.content:
# ଯୁକ୍ତାକ୍ଷର (Conjunct Consonants)

When consonants collide with no vowel between, Odia fuses them into a
**ଯୁକ୍ତାକ୍ଷର** (conjunct). The virama **୍** signals the fusion:
**କ୍** = bare "k".

## Everyday conjuncts

| Conjunct | Word | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| କ୍କ | ପକ୍କା | ripe/certain |
| ତ୍ତ | ଉତ୍ତର | answer |
| ନ୍ଦ | ଆନନ୍ଦ | joy |
| ମ୍ବ | ଅମ୍ବ | mango |
| ଜ୍ଞ | ବିଜ୍ଞାନ | science |
| ସ୍ଥ | ସ୍ଥାନ | place |
| ର୍ଯ | କାର୍ଯ୍ୟ | work/deed |

## The special ର rules

**ର** before a consonant becomes the diagonal **ର୍** above:
**ଧର୍ମ** (dharma) — see the slanted ra on top. **ର** after a consonant
becomes **୍ର** below: **ପ୍ରେମ** (prema, love).

## Reading drill

Try: **ସ୍ୱାଗତ** (swāgata, welcome), **ପ୍ରୀତି** (prīti, love),
**ଉତ୍ସବ** (utsaba, festival), **ଗ୍ରନ୍ଥ** (grantha, book).

> Like all its sister scripts, high-frequency conjuncts become
> sight-shapes. Ten minutes a day and ତ୍ତ, ନ୍ଦ, ସ୍ଥ stop being
> puzzles.
## Mini-practice

Read: ଉତ୍ତର, ଆନନ୍ଦ, ଅମ୍ବ, ବିଜ୍ଞାନ, ସ୍ଥାନ, କାର୍ଯ୍ୟ, ଧର୍ମ, ପ୍ରେମ. Count the conjuncts across all
eight words (nine: ତ୍ତ, ନ୍ଦ, ମ୍ବ, ଜ୍ଞ, ସ୍ଥ, ର୍ଯ, ର୍ମ, ପ୍ର). Sight-shapes
come fast — ତ୍ତ and ନ୍ଦ you have already seen three times.

lessons.title: ନମସ୍କାର · Greetings
lessons.subtitle: Namaskāra and the warm Odia hello
lessons.content:
# ନମସ୍କାର (Greetings)

**ନମସ୍କାର** (namaskāra) is the standard Odia greeting — respectful,
timeless, works with anyone at any hour. Friends say **କେମନ ଅଛ?**
("how are you?") straight away — Odia warmth skips small talk.

## The greeting set

| Odia | Transliteration | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| ନମସ୍କାର | namaskāra | hello |
| ଶୁଭ ପ୍ରଭାତ | śubha prabhāta | good morning |
| ଶୁଭ ରାତ୍ରି | śubha rātri | good night |
| ଧନ୍ୟବାଦ | dhanyabāda | thank you |
| ମାଫ କରନ୍ତୁ | māpha karantu | sorry / excuse me |
| ଆସନ୍ତୁ | āsantu | please come |

## Asking how someone is

- **କେମିତି ଅଛନ୍ତି?** — How are you? (respectful)
- **କେମନ ଅଛ?** — How are you? (friend/child)
- Answer: **ମୁଁ ଭଲ ଅଛି.** — I am well. (**ଭଲ** = good/fine)
- **ଆପଣ କେମିତି ଅଛନ୍ତି?** — And you (respectful)?

## Goodbye

**ଆସିବି** (āsibi) — "I will come (again)" — the standard farewell,
framed as returning. Reply **ଆସନ୍ତୁ ଆସନ୍ତୁ** (come, come!) or simply
**ଭଲ ରୁହନ୍ତୁ** (be well).

> Odia hospitality is famous: entering a home you will be offered water
> first. **ପାଣି ପିଅନ୍ତୁ** (please drink water) is said before hello.
## Mini-practice

The full exchange, out loud: ନମସ୍କାର! → କେମିତି ଅଛନ୍ତି? → ମୁଁ ଭଲ ଅଛି,
ଆପଣ? → ଭଲ, ଧନ୍ୟବାଦ! Then the closer: ଆସିବି! → ଆସନ୍ତୁ ଆସନ୍ତୁ! Five
sentences that carry a whole doorway conversation in Odisha —
memorise them as one breath, not five lines.

lessons.title: ମୋର ନାମ · Introductions
lessons.subtitle: My name is…, asking back, and the learner's lines
lessons.content:
# ମୋର ନାମ (Introductions)

## Saying your name

**ମୋର ନାମ ରାହୁଲ.** (Mora nāma Rāhula.) — My name is Rahul.
**ମୋର** (my) + **ନାମ** (name). Ask back: **ଆପଣଙ୍କ ନାମ କଣ?**
(Āpaṇaṅka nāma kṇa?) — What is your name? (respectful; **କଣ** = what)
To a friend: **ତୁମ ନାମ କଣ?**

## Where from

- **ଆପଣ କେଉଁଠୁ ଆସିଛନ୍ତି?** — Where have you come from?
- **ମୁଁ ଭୁବନେଶ୍ୱରରୁ ଆସିଛି.** — I have come from Bhubaneswar.
  (**-ରୁ** = from)
- **ମୁଁ ଓଡ଼ିଶାର.** — I am of/from Odisha. (**-ର** = of)

## The learner's toolkit

| Odia | Transliteration | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| ମୁଁ ଓଡ଼ିଆ ଶିଖୁଛି | muṃ oṛiā śikhuchi | I am learning Odia |
| ଧୀରେ କହନ୍ତୁ | dhīre kahantu | please say (it) slowly |
| ମୁଁ ବୁଝିପାରିଲି ନାହିଁ | muṃ bujhipārili nāhiṃ | I didn't understand |
| ପୁଣି କୁହ | puṇi khu | say (it) again |

**ଶିଖିବା** (śikhibā, to learn) is your verb of the year — and
**ଧୀରେ ଧୀରେ** (slowly, slowly) is how everything worthwhile happens.
## Mini-practice

Fill in and say: ମୋର ନାମ ___. ମୁଁ ___ ରୁ ଆସିଛି (from ___). ମୁଁ ଓଡ଼ିଆ
ଶିଖୁଛି. Then ask: ଆପଣଙ୍କ ନାମ କଣ? ଆପଣ କେଉଁଠୁ ଆସିଛନ୍ତି? Keep the
honorific -ନ୍ତି/-ଙ୍କ with strangers — ଆପଣଙ୍କ ନାମ (your, hon., name).
Three loops of the intro and it stops feeling like a script.

lessons.title: ପରିବାର · Family
lessons.subtitle: The family words and the bhāi/bhaujā address culture
lessons.content:
# ପରିବାର (Family)

## Core words

| Odia | Transliteration | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| ମାଆ | māā | mother |
| ବାପା | bāpā | father |
| ଭାଇ | bhāi | brother |
| ଭଉଣୀ | bhauṇī | sister |
| ଜ୍ୟେଷ୍ଠ ଭାଇ | jyeṣṭha bhāi | elder brother |
| ସାନ ଭାଇ | sāna bhāi | younger brother |
| ବଡ଼ ଭଉଣୀ | baḍa bhauṇī | elder sister |
| ଆଜା | ājā | grandfather |
| ଆଜି | āji | grandmother |
| ପୁଅ | pua | son |
| ଝିଅ | jhiā | daughter |

Age is packed into modifiers: **ବଡ଼** (big/elder) and **ସାନ** (small/
younger) prefix the plain word — elder brother **ବଡ଼ ଭାଇ**, younger
**ସାନ ଭାଇ**. (Odia does have a dedicated elder-brother word too:
**ଦାଦା** / **ଭାଇଡ଼ା**.)

## Address culture

**ଭାଇ** (brother) and **ମାଉସୀ/କାକୀ** (auntie) are used for strangers
warmly — a shopkeeper is **ଭାଇ**, an older lady **ମାଉସୀ**. Add
respectful **-ନ୍ତୁ** verb endings and you are instantly polite.

## Sentences

- **ଇହା ମୋର ମାଆ.** — This is my mother.
- **ମୋର ଜଣେ ଭଉଣୀ ଅଛି.** — I have one sister.
- **ମୋ ପରିବାର ବଡ଼.** — My family is big.
- **ମୋ ଆଜି ମହାପ୍ରଭୁଙ୍କ ଭକ୍ତ.** — My grandmother is a devotee of the Lord
  (of Puri — expect Jagannath in every Odia family conversation).
## Mini-practice

Map YOUR family: ମାଆ, ବାପା, ଭାଇ/ଭଉଣୀ (with ବଡ଼/ସାନ modifiers),
ଆଜା/ଆଜି. Then two sentences: ଇହା ମୋର ___. ମୋର ଜଣେ ___ ଅଛି. Notice
ଭାଇ/ମାଉସୀ work for strangers too — the shopkeeper is ଭାଇ, the
lady next door is ମାଉସୀ. Kinship as politeness, the Odia way.

lessons.title: ଗଣନା · Numbers
lessons.subtitle: Odia numerals ୦–୯ and counting to one hundred
lessons.content:
# ଗଣନା (Numbers)

## The numerals

| Digit | Odia | Name | Digit | Odia | Name |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | ୦ | ଶୂନ | 5 | ୫ | ପାଞ୍ଚ |
| 1 | ୧ | ଏକ | 6 | ୬ | ଛଅ |
| 2 | ୨ | ଦୁଇ | 7 | ୭ | ସାତ |
| 3 | ୩ | ତିନି | 8 | ୮ | ଆଠ |
| 4 | ୪ | ଚାରି | 9 | ୯ | ନଅ |

Bus boards and market slates use these digits; learn the shapes beside
0–9.

## Tens to a hundred

- 10 **ଦଶ** (daśa), 20 **କୁଡ଼ି** (kuṛi), 30 **ତିରିଶ**
  (tiriśa), 40 **ଚାଳିଶ** (cāḷiśa), 50 **ପଚାଶ** (pacāśa),
  100 **ଶହ** (śaha).
- 21: **କୁଡ଼ି ଏକ** / common form **କୋଡ଼ିଏକ** — twenty-one.

## Money and count phrases

- **କେତେ?** (kete?) — how much?
- **ପାଞ୍ଚ ଟଙ୍କା** — five rupees. (**ଟଙ୍କା** = rupee/money)
- **ମୋର ପଚାଶ ଟଙ୍କା ଅଛି.** — I have fifty rupees.
- Age: **ମୋର କୁଡ଼ି ବର୍ଷ ବୟସ ହେଲା.** — I turned twenty.

> Tens words are irregular (kuṛi, tiriśa, cāḷiśa…) like English
> "eleven/twelve" — memorise them as words, not arithmetic.
## Mini-practice

Count ଏକ → ଦଶ aloud, then the tens: କୁଡ଼ି, ତିରିଶ, ଚାଳିଶ, ପଚାଶ, ଶହ.
Market drill: କେତେ ଦାମ? → ପଚାଶ ଟଙ୍କା → ଅଳ୍ପ କମ୍ କରନ୍ତୁ! → ସରି. The
tens words are irregular like English "eleven" — memorise them as
words, and haggling becomes arithmetic you already know.

lessons.title: ସରଳ ବାକ୍ୟ · Simple Sentences
lessons.subtitle: SOV order and ଅଛି / ନାହିଁ — the sentence engine
lessons.content:
# ସରଳ ବାକ୍ୟ (Simple Sentences)

Odia is **SOV**: subject → object → verb. The verb closes the sentence,
always.

## Word order

- **ମୁଁ ଭାତ ଖାଉଛି.** — I am eating rice. (I rice eating-am)
- **ସେ ବହି ପଢ଼ୁଛି.** — He/she reads a book.
- **ପିଲାମାନେ ଖେଳୁଛନ୍ତି.** — The children are playing.
  (plural verb -ନ୍ତି)

## ଅଛି — "there is / have"

- **ପାଣି ଅଛି.** — There is water.
- **ମୋର ସମୟ ଅଛି.** — I have time. (to-me time is)
- Negative: **ନାହିଁ** — **ମୋର ସମୟ ନାହିଁ.** — I have no time.

## Location words

**ରେ** = in/at: **ଘରେ** (at home), **ବଜାରରେ** (in the market). "On" is
**ଉପରେ**, "under" **ତଳେ**, "near" **ପାଖରେ**.

- **ବହିଟି ଟେବୁଲ ଉପରେ ଅଛି.** — The book is on the table.
- **ମାଆ ଘରେ ଅଛନ୍ତି.** — Mother is at home. (respectful -ନ୍ତି)

## Everyday verbs

**ଯିବା** (go), **ଆସିବା** (come), **ଖାଇବା** (eat), **ପିଇବା** (drink),
**ଶୋଇବା** (sleep), **କାମ କରିବା** (work). Verb ends: -ଉଛି (I, right
now), -ଉଛ (you), -ଉଛନ୍ତି (they/respect).
## Mini-practice

Swap nouns in the frames: ମୁଁ ___ ଖାଉଛି (ଭାତ/ଫଳ/ରୁଟି). ସେ ___ ପଢ଼ୁଛି
(ବହି/ଖବର). ବହିଟି ___ ଅଛି (ଟେବୁଲ ଉପରେ/ଘରେ). Ending drill: ଖାଉଛି (I),
ଖାଉଛ (you-fr), ଖାଉଛନ୍ତି (they/resp). Verb last, ending follows the
person — say each frame once and the SOV rhythm locks.

lessons.title: ପ୍ରଶ୍ନ · Questions
lessons.subtitle: କଣ, କିଏ, କେଉଁଠି, କେବେ — question words stay in place
lessons.content:
# ପ୍ରଶ୍ନ (Questions)

## The question words

| Odia | Transliteration | Meaning | Example |
|---|---|---|---|
| କଣ | kṇa | what | ଇହା କଣ? — What is this? |
| କିଏ | kiē | who | ସେ କିଏ? — Who is he/she? |
| କେଉଁଠି | keuṃṭhi | where | ବସ୍ କେଉଁଠି? — Where is the bus? |
| କେବେ | kebe | when | କେବେ ଆସିବ? — When will (you) come? |
| କେତେ | kete | how much | କେତେ ଦାମ? — How much price? |
| କିପରି | kipari | how | କିପରି ଯିବି? — How to go? |

Question words sit where the answer sits — "you where-going?" is the
Odia way: **ଆପଣ କେଉଁଠି ଯାଉଛନ୍ତି?**

## Yes / no

Add **-କି** at the start or **-ତା?** endings: **ଆସିବ କି?** — will you
come? **ଠିକ୍ ଅଛି ତା?** — it's okay, right? Tone does the rest.

## The answer kit

- **ହଁ** (haṃ) — yes. **ନା / ନାହିଁ** — no / not-have.
- **ଠିକ୍ ଅଛି** — it's fine (Odia's all-purpose "okay").
- **ମୋର ଜଣା ନାହିଁ** — I don't know (lit. "it is not known to me").
## Mini-practice

Answer, don't just ask: ଇହା କଣ? → ଇହା ବହି. ବସ୍ କେଉଁଠି? → ସେଠାରେ!
କେବେ ଆସିବ? → ଏବେ (now). କେତେ ଦାମ? → ଚାଳିଶ ଟଙ୍କା. Question words sit
where the answer sits — practise each question with its answer so
the slot habit forms in both directions.

lessons.title: ନିଷେଧ · Negation
lessons.subtitle: ନାହିଁ, ନୁହେଁ, ନା — the no-family with three jobs
lessons.content:
# ନିଷେଧ (Negation)

## ନାହିଁ — "is not there / don't have"

- **ପାଣି ନାହିଁ.** — There is no water.
- **ମୋର ଟଙ୍କା ନାହିଁ.** — I have no money.
- **ଆଜି ନାହିଁ** — not today.

## ନୁହେଁ — "is not" (identity)

- **ଇହା ଦୁଧ ନୁହେଁ, ପାଣି.** — This is not milk, (it is) water.
- **ମୁଁ ଡାକ୍ତର ନୁହେଁ.** — I am not a doctor.

## Verb negation

Verbs negate with **ନାହିଁ** after the participle or by negative verb
forms: **ଯାଉଛି** (I am going) → **ଯାଉନାହିଁ** (I am not going);
future **ଯିବି** → **ଯିବି ନାହିଁ / ଯିବିନି** (won't go).

| Positive | Negative | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| ଅଛି | ନାହିଁ | there is / there isn't |
| ହେବ | ହେବ ନାହିଁ | will happen / won't |
| ପାରିବି | ପାରିବି ନାହିଁ | can / cannot |
| ଦରକାର | ଦରକାର ନାହିଁ | needed / not needed |

> **ନା, ନା, ଦରକାର ନାହିଁ** ("no, no, not needed") is the polite shop
> refusal — with a smile it ends any upsell kindly.
## Mini-practice

Pick the right no: no water? → ପାଣି ନାହିଁ. Not milk? → ଇହା ଦୁଧ
ନୁହେଁ. Am not going? → ମୁଁ ଯାଉନାହିଁ. Not needed? → ଦରକାର ନାହିଁ. Three
no's, three jobs — ନାହିଁ existence, ନୁହେଁ identity, verb +
ନାହିଁ/ନିନି for actions. The shop refusal: ନା, ଦରକାର ନାହିଁ.

lessons.title: ଦୈନିକ କାର୍ଯ୍ୟ · Daily Routine
lessons.subtitle: Clocks, meals, and the verbs of an ordinary Odisha day
lessons.content:
# ଦୈନିକ କାର୍ଯ୍ୟ (Daily Routine)

## Time

- **କେତେ ସମୟ ହେଲା?** — What time is it? (how much time became)
- **ଛଅ ଟା ହେଲା.** — It's six o'clock. (**-ଟା** is the clock-tap ending)
- **ସକାଳ** morning, **ମଧ୍ୟାହ୍ନ** noon, **ସନ୍ଧ୍ୟା** evening,
  **ରାତି** night. **ସକାଳ ସାତ ଟାରୁ** — from seven in the morning.

## A narrated day

- **ମୁଁ ସକାଳ ଛଅ ଟାରେ ଉଠେ.** — I wake at six in the morning.
- **ଚା ପିଏ.** — I drink tea. (Odia mornings run on ଚା)
- **ଆଠ ଟାରେ କାମକୁ ଯାଏ.** — At eight I go to work.
- **ରାତି ଦଶ ଟାରେ ଶୋଏ.** — At ten at night I sleep.

Note the habitual endings: **ଉଠେ, ପିଏ, ଯାଏ, ଶୋଏ** — the plain
present for daily facts.

## Meals, Odisha style

**ଭାତ** rice (the center of everything), **ଦାଲମା**, **ମାଛ ଭଜା**
(fried fish), **ପଖାଳ** (pakhāḷa — fermented water-rice,
Odisha's summer icon).

- **ଭୋଜନ ହେଲା?** — Is the meal ready/done?
- **ବହୁତ ସ୍ୱାଦ!** — Very tasty!
## Mini-practice

Narrate YOUR day in five sentences: ମୁଁ ସକାଳ ___ ଟାରେ ଉଠେ. ଚା ପିଏ.
___ ଟାରେ କାମକୁ ଯାଏ. ସନ୍ଧ୍ୟାରେ ଘରକୁ ଆସେ. ରାତି ___ ଟାରେ ଶୋଏ. The
habitual endings (ଉଠେ, ପିଏ, ଯାଏ, ଶୋଏ) are for facts that repeat —
your routine, by definition. Say it daily; you are living the
grammar.

lessons.title: ସର୍ବନାମ · Pronouns
lessons.subtitle: The pronoun set and the respectful -ନ୍ତି rule
lessons.content:
# ସର୍ବନାମ (Pronouns)

## The set

| Odia | Transliteration | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| ମୁଁ | muṃ | I |
| ତୁ | tu | you (very intimate) |
| ତୁମେ | tumē | you (friendly) |
| ଆପଣ | āpaṇa | you (respectful) |
| ସେ | sē | he/she |
| ଏହା | ehā | it/this |
| ଆମେ | āmē | we |
| ସେମାନେ | sēmānē | they |

## The three you's

**ତୁ** (very close/child), **ତୁମେ** (friend), **ଆପଣ** (respect —
strangers, elders, customers). Verb endings follow: **ଯାଉଛ** (you-int
go) / **ଯାଉଛ** (you-fr go) / **ଯାଉଛନ୍ତି** (you-resp go). When in
doubt: **ଆପଣ** + -ନ୍ତି never insults anyone.

## ସେ covers both he and she

Odia **ସେ** is gender-free; if needed specify **ପୁଅଟି** (the boy) /
**ଝିଅଟି** (the girl) or a name. Objects have no grammatical gender
either — tables and books are all **ଏହା**. (Gender-driven declensions,
the classic European headache, do not exist.)

## Verb agreement preview

**ମୁଁ କରୁଛି / ତୁମେ କରୁଛ / ସେ କରୁଛି / ଆମେ କରୁଛୁ / ସେମାନେ କରୁଛନ୍ତି** —
I/you/you/you/are doing. One verb, five endings, all regular.
## Mini-practice

Climb the you-ladder with one verb: ତୁ ଯାଉଛ (intimate), ତୁମେ
ଯାଉଛ (friendly), ଆପଣ ଯାଉଛନ୍ତି (respectful). Then conjugate କରିବା
across the full set: ମୁଁ କରୁଛି, ସେ କରୁଛି, ଆମେ କରୁଛୁ, ସେମାନେ
କରୁଛନ୍ତି. Remember: ସେ covers he AND she; objects are all ଏହା —
no gender grammar anywhere.

lessons.title: କାଳ · Tenses
lessons.subtitle: Present progressive, habitual, past, future — କରିବା as the map
lessons.content:
# କାଳ (Tenses)

## The four-time map on କରିବା (do)

| Tense | Form | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| Present progressive | କରୁଛି | I am doing |
| Habitual present | କରେ | (I) do (daily) |
| Past | କଲି | I did |
| Future | କରିବି | (you) will do |

Progressive = stem + **-ଉଛି/-ଉଛ/-ଉଛନ୍ତି**; habitual = **-ଏ**-family
(କରେ, ଖାଏ, ଯାଏ); past = **-ିଲି/-ିଲା/-ିଲେ** (କଲି, ଖାଇଲି, ଗଲି);
future = **-ିବି/-ିବ/-ିବା** (କରିବି, ଯିବି).

## Same verb, four sentences

- **ମୁଁ ଏବେ ଚା ପିଉଛି.** — I am drinking tea now.
- **ମୁଁ ପ୍ରତିଦିନ ଚା ପିଏ.** — I drink tea every day.
- **ଗତକାଲ ମୁଁ ଚା ପିଇଲି.** — Yesterday I drank tea.
- **ଆସନ୍ତାକାଲି ମୁଁ ପୁରୀକୁ ଯିବି.** — Tomorrow I will go to Puri.

## Time anchors

**ଆଜି** (today), **ଗତକାଲ** (yesterday), **ଆସନ୍ତାକାଲି** (tomorrow),
**ପ୍ରତିଦିନ** (every day), **ଏବେ** (now), **ପରେ** (later).

> Past forms twist: ଯିବା (go) → ଗଲି (went); ଆସିବା (come) → ଆସିଲି
> (came); ଖାଇବା (eat) → ଖାଇଲି. Learn past forms as partner-words.
## Mini-practice

Four tenses of ଖାଇବା (eat): ଖାଉଛି (am eating), ଖାଏ (eats), ଖାଇଲି
(ate), ଖାଇବି (will eat). Build one sentence each with time anchors:
ଏବେ, ପ୍ରତିଦିନ, ଗତକାଲ, ଆସନ୍ତାକାଲି. Past-form pairs to memorise:
ଯିବା→ଗଲି, ଆସିବା→ଆସିଲି, କରିବା→କଲି.

lessons.title: କାରକ · Case Endings
lessons.subtitle: To, from, in, with — the suffixes that do prepositions' job
lessons.content:
# କାରକ (Case Endings)

## The big six

| Ending | Meaning | Example |
|---|---|---|
| -କୁ | to | ପୁରୀକୁ (to Puri) |
| -ରୁ | from | ଭୁବନେଶ୍ୱରରୁ (from Bhubaneswar) |
| -ରେ | in/at | ବଜାରରେ (in the market) |
| ସହ / -ପାଖରେ | with | ବନ୍ଧୁ ସହ (with a friend) |
| -ର | 's / of | ରାହୁଲର ବହି (Rahul's book) |
| object: bare or -କୁ | — | ଭାତ ଖାଅ / ଭାତକୁ ଖାଅ |

## Fusion patterns

**ଘର + କୁ → ଘରକୁ** (homeward); **ଘର + ରେ → ଘରେ** (at home); after
consonant-final nouns the -ର/-ରେ/-ରୁ slip a **-ର-** or **-ୟ-** in:
**ଭୁବନେଶ୍ୱର + ରୁ → ଭୁବନେଶ୍ୱର**ରୁ. Expect glue sounds — they are
regular.

## Sentences to steal

- **ମୁଁ ବଜାରକୁ ଯାଉଛି.** — I'm going to the market.
- **ସେମାନେ ଦିଲ୍ଲୀରୁ ଆସିଲେ.** — They came from Delhi.
- **ଇହା ମୋ ଆଜିଙ୍କ ଘର.** — This is my grandmother's house.
- **ମୁଁ ବନ୍ଧୁ ସହ ସିନେମାକୁ ଗଲି.** — I went to the movies with a friend.

> The **-ଙ୍କ** honorific possessive (**ମାଆଙ୍କ, ଆପଣଙ୍କ**) marks
> respected owners — ମାଆଙ୍କ ନାମ = mother's name (hon.).
## Mini-practice

Slot the endings: ପୁରୀ___ ଯାଉଛି (→ -କୁ), ଭୁବନେଶ୍ୱର___ ଆସିଲି (→
-ରରୁ? careful — ଭୁବନେଶ୍ୱରରୁ, glue -ର- appears), ବଜାର___ ଅଛି (→
-ରେ), ରାହୁଲ___ ବହି (→ -ର). Watch the glue sounds with
consonant-final nouns — ଭୁବନେଶ୍ୱରରୁ carries a doubled ର. Fusion is
regular once you expect it.

lessons.title: ଆଦର · Politeness
lessons.subtitle: The -ନ୍ତି respect rule, soft imperatives, and Odia titles
lessons.content:
# ଆଦର (Politeness & Honorifics)

## The -ନ୍ତି rule

Respect = plural-style verb ending **-ନ୍ତି** + plural pronoun **ଆପଣ/
ସେମାନେ**: **ସେ ଆସିଲା** (he came) → **ଆପଣ ଆସିଲେ / ମାଆ ଆସିଲେ** (mother,
hon., came). Possessive gets **-ଙ୍କ**: **ଆପଣଙ୍କ ନାମ** (your, hon., name).

## Soft imperative ladder

| Command | To whom |
|---|---|
| ଆସ (come) | children, very close |
| ଆସ (come, friendly) | friends, siblings |
| ଆସନ୍ତୁ (kindly come) | respectful |

The same ladder on sit: **ବସ / ବସନ୍ତୁ** — sit / please sit. A shop line:
**ଆସନ୍ତୁ, ବସନ୍ତୁ, କଣ ଦରକାର?** — Come, sit, what do you need?

## Softeners

- **ଧୀରେ** — slowly: **ଧୀରେ କହନ୍ତୁ** — please speak slowly.
- **ଏକ ମୁହୂର୍ତ୍ତ** — one moment.
- **ଦୟାକରି** — please (formal; notices use it).
- **ଅଳ୍ପ** — a little: **ଅଳ୍ପ କମ୍ କରନ୍ତୁ** — reduce (the price) a little.

## Titles you'll hear

**ଭାଇ** (brother — any friendly male), **ମାଉସୀ/କାକୀ** (auntie),
**ବଡ଼ ଭାଇ/ଦାଦା** (elder brother), **ସାର୍/ମେଡାମ** offices. The
honorific **-ନ୍ତୁ/-ଙ୍କ** endings slot into every sentence you already
know.
## Mini-practice

Climb the ladder: ଆସ → ଆସନ୍ତୁ (come). ବସ → ବସନ୍ତୁ (sit). କହ →
କହନ୍ତୁ (say). Then the honorific possessive: ମାଆ___ ନାମ (→
ମାଆଙ୍କ ନାମ), ଆପଣ___ ନାମ (→ ଆପଣଙ୍କ ନାମ). Soften: ପାଣି ଦିଅ →
ଦୟାକରି ପାଣି ଦିଅନ୍ତୁ. The -ନ୍ତୁ/-ଙ୍କ pair is Odia respect in two
endings.

lessons.title: କଥୋପକଥନ · Conversations
lessons.subtitle: At the market and at a friend's door — two real dialogues
lessons.content:
# କଥୋପକଥନ (Conversations)

## At the market

> **ଦୋକାନୀ:** ଆସନ୍ତୁ ଆସନ୍ତୁ, କଣ ଦରକାର?
> **ଆପଣ:** ଟମାଟୋ କେତେ ଦାମ?
> **ଦୋକାନୀ:** କିଲୋ ଚାଳିଶ ଟଙ୍କା.
> **ଆପଣ:** ଅଳ୍ପ କମ୍ କରନ୍ତୁ!
> **ଦୋକାନୀ:** ସରି, ତିରିଶ ଟଙ୍କା ଦିଅନ୍ତୁ.
> **ଆପଣ:** ଠିକ୍ ଅଛି, ଦୁଇ କିଲୋ ଦିଅନ୍ତୁ.

Translation: "Come, come — what do you need?" / "How much are
tomatoes?" / "Forty rupees a kilo." / "Please reduce a little!" /
"Okay, give thirty." / "Fine, give me two kilos."

## At a friend's door

> **ଆପଣ:** ନମସ୍କାର! ମାଆ ଘରେ ଅଛନ୍ତି କି?
> **ସେ:** ଅଛନ୍ତି. ଭିତରକୁ ଆସନ୍ତୁ.
> **ଆପଣ:** ପରେ ଆସିବି, ଏବେ କାମକୁ ଯିବି.
> **ସେ:** ଠିକ୍ ଅଛି. ଆସିବି ଆସିବି!

Translation: "Hello! Is mother at home?" / "She is. Please come in." /
"I'll come later — I have to go to work now." / "Okay. Do come back!"

## Notice

- **-କି** flips a statement into a yes/no question.
- **କଣ ଦରକାର?** — "what is needed?" — the standard shop opener.
- **ଆସିବି ଆସିବି** — "I'll come, I'll come" — the farewell that promises
  return.
## Mini-practice

Act both roles of the market dialogue from memory, then change the
item: ଆଳୁ (potato), ପିଆଜ (onion), ମାଛ (fish). Change the numbers
too. The frames — କଣ ଦରକାର? / କେତେ ଦାମ? / ଅଳ୍ପ କମ୍ କରନ୍ତୁ! / ଠିକ୍
ଅଛି — never change; nouns and numerals rotate.

lessons.title: ଅନୁଚ୍ଛେଦ ପଠନ · Reading a Paragraph
lessons.subtitle: A postcard from Puri — real sentences, familiar words
lessons.content:
# ଅନୁଚ୍ଛେଦ ପଠନ (Reading a Paragraph)

## The text

**ପୁରୀ ଯାତ୍ରା**

ଗତ ସପ୍ତାହ ମୁଁ ପୁରୀକୁ ଗଲି. ଭୁବନେଶ୍ୱରରୁ ଟ୍ରେନରେ ଏକ ଘଣ୍ଟା. ସକାଳେ ସମୁଦ୍ର
କୂଳରେ ଚାଲିଲି — ଢେଉ ଆଉ ବାଲି! ମନ୍ଦିର ଦର୍ଶନ କଲି. ମଧ୍ୟାହ୍ନରେ ମାଛ ଭାତ ଖାଇଲି —
ବହୁତ ସ୍ୱାଦ! ସନ୍ଧ୍ୟାରେ ସମୁଦ୍ରରେ ସୂର୍ଯ୍ୟାସ୍ତ ଦେଖିଲି.

## Sentence by sentence

1. **ଗତ ସପ୍ତାହ ମୁଁ ପୁରୀକୁ ଗଲି.** — Last week I went to Puri.
   (ଗତ = past; -କୁ = to; ଗଲି = went)
2. **ଭୁବନେଶ୍ୱରରୁ ଟ୍ରେନରେ ଏକ ଘଣ୍ଟା.** — One hour by train from
   Bhubaneswar. (-ରୁ from; -ରେ by/in)
3. **ସକାଳେ ସମୁଦ୍ର କୂଳରେ ଚାଲିଲି.** — In the morning (I) walked on the
   seashore. (ସମୁଦ୍ର = sea; କୂଳ = shore)
4. **ଢେଉ ଆଉ ବାଲି!** — Waves and sand! (ଆଉ = and)
5. **ମନ୍ଦିର ଦର୍ଶନ କଲି.** — Had darshan of the temple. (ଦର୍ଶନ = holy
   viewing — the culturally right verb for temples)
6. **ମଧ୍ୟାହ୍ନରେ ମାଛ ଭାତ ଖାଇଲି — ବହୁତ ସ୍ୱାଦ!** — At noon ate fish-rice —
   very tasty!

## Comprehension check

- Travel time? **ଏକ ଘଣ୍ଟା** (one hour).
- What was eaten? **ମାଛ ଭାତ**.
- The holy-viewing word: **ଦର୍ଶନ**.

You just read a real paragraph — every word came from your earlier
lessons. That is the ladder working.
## Mini-practice

Re-read the Puri paragraph aloud twice, then rebuild from memory:
last-week / I / Puri-to / went. Where does ଗଲି land? (At the end —
every sentence.) Then edit one detail and re-say: ଟ୍ରେନରେ → ବସ୍
ରେ (by bus). Editing your own sentences is the last skill before
fluency.

lessons.title: ପ୍ରବାଦ · Proverbs
lessons.subtitle: Four Odia proverbs and the culture inside them
lessons.content:
# ପ୍ରବାଦ (Proverbs & Culture)

Proverbs (**ପ୍ରବାଦ**) are grammar, vocabulary and worldview in one
line. Four classics:

## 1. ନିଜ ଘର ତୁଳନାରେ ପର ଘର ସ୍ୱର୍ଗ

"Another's house seems heaven compared to one's own." — the grass is
greener on the other side. **ନିଜ** (own), **ପର** (other's),
**ଘର** (house), **ସ୍ୱର୍ଗ** (heaven), **ତୁଳନା** (comparison).

## 2. ଯାହା କାମ, ସେହି ସାଜ

"That which is useful is the true adornment." — function is beauty; a
craftsman's proverb from Odisha's artisan culture. Apply it to
learning: useful words first, fancy words later. **କାମ** (work/use),
**ସାଜ** (adornment).

## 3. ଅଳ୍ପ ଜ୍ଞାନ ବିଷ ସମ

"A little knowledge is equal to poison." — half-knowledge misleads.
**ଅଳ୍ପ** (little), **ଜ୍ଞାନ** (knowledge), **ବିଷ** (poison),
**ସମ** (equal to). A perfect studying proverb — and you now hold
non-ଅଳ୍ପ script knowledge.

## 4. ଗଛରୁ ଫଳ ତଳକୁ ଖସେ, ଉପରକୁ କେବେ ନାହିଁ

"Fruit falls from the tree downward, never upward." — everything
naturally settles; rising needs effort. **ଗଛ** (tree), **ଫଳ**
(fruit), **ଖସେ** (falls), **ତଳ** (down), **ଉପର** (up). The engine's
review scheduler exists precisely to fight this proverb.

> Proverbs keep SOV order too — read each aloud twice; the rhythm is
> half the memory.
## Mini-practice

Match proverb to situation: someone envies another's home (→ ନିଜ
ଘର ତୁଳନାରେ ପର ଘର ସ୍ୱର୍ଗ). You skipped half the lesson and got
confused (→ ଅଳ୍ପ ଜ୍ଞାନ ବିଷ ସମ). You feel practice slipping (→ ଗଛରୁ
ଫଳ ତଳକୁ ଖସେ, ଉପରକୁ କେବେ ନାହିଁ — that is why reviews exist). Say
each with its story.

lessons.title: ପୁନରାବୃତ୍ତି · Review
lessons.subtitle: The whole beginner journey — ଅ to ହ in one page
lessons.content:
# ପୁନରାବୃତ୍ତି (Review)

## Script ladder

- Vowels **ସ୍ୱର** (11), consonant grid **ବ୍ୟଞ୍ଜନ**, vowel signs
  **ମାତ୍ରା**, conjuncts **ଯୁକ୍ତାକ୍ଷର**.
- The dotted flap pair **ଡ଼/ଢ଼** — in the language's own name!
- Left-side ି sign; top-diagonal ର୍; below ୍ର.

## Words banked

ନମସ୍କାର, ଧନ୍ୟବାଦ, ମାଫ କରନ୍ତୁ, କେମିତି ଅଛନ୍ତି, ଭଲ ଅଛି, ମୋର ନାମ…,
ମାଆ, ବାପା, ଭାଇ, ଭଉଣୀ, ଏକ…ଦଶ, ଶହ, କେତେ, ଟଙ୍କା, ଭାତ, ଚା, ପାଣି,
ମାଛ, ପଖାଳ.

## Structures banked

- **ଅଛି / ନାହିଁ** existence; **ନୁହେଁ** identity negation.
- Question words in place + **-କି** yes/no.
- Four tenses: -ଉଛି / -ଏ / -ିଲି / -ିବି.
- Cases: -କୁ, -ରୁ, -ରେ, ସହ, -ର, honorific -ଙ୍କ.
- Respect ladder: ତୁ → ତୁମେ → ଆପଣ + -ନ୍ତି.

## Self-check

1. Finish **ମୋର ନାମ ___** with your name; ask mine respectfully.
2. Order two kilos of tomatoes and haggle once.
3. Say one past-tense sentence with **ଯିବା** (go).
4. Read **ଓଡ଼ିଆ**, **ସ୍ୱାଗତ**, **କାର୍ଯ୍ୟ** aloud — dotted ଡ଼ included.

All four? The adaptive engine now schedules your reviews and lifts the
next rung. ଶୁଭକାମନା! (Best wishes!)
## Mini-practice

The four self-checks — do them NOW, aloud: 1) ମୋର ନାମ ___ + ask
back respectfully, 2) haggle two kilos of tomatoes, 3) one
past-tense sentence with ଯିବା, 4) read ଓଡ଼ିଆ, ସ୍ୱାଗତ, କାର୍ଯ୍ୟ (dotted
ଡ଼ included). All smooth? Your practice engine moves to
maintenance mode — short, spaced reviews of exactly what dipped.
